title: Transient provider failures from CLI workers map to 'unavailable' (breaker), not 'quota' (IMP-0016)
summary: The operator asked to continue autonomous development past the ORCH-0024 hold (DEC-0027), which scoped the pass as a maintenance check. Reading the failure path during that check found a routing defect: QUOTA_PATTERN contained 'overloaded', so a single transient Anthropic 529 surfaced by the Claude CLI opened a one-hour machine-wide cooldown shared by every run, delegate and eval, and 5xx/network errors fell to process_error, which the breaker never counts. The CLIs retry these internally before surfacing them, so they now map to 'unavailable', matching HTTPAPIAdapter (5xx/529 -> unavailable): the node fails over as before (unavailable is a PROVIDER_FAILURE), but the machine-wide effect is the existing breaker (3 in 10 min -> 15 min cooldown) instead of an hour-long cooldown after one blip. Quota and invalid_model keep precedence. Status codes count only next to an HTTP/API/status cue, so bare numbers in prose stay process_error. This also covers RT-06 for CLI workers without engine-side backoff: the CLIs already back off in-process, and adding a second retry layer would create the nested retry loops RT-08 warns about. The ORCH-0019 target (real-model injection, EXP-0008) stays operator-gated per DEC-0025/FND-0013 and was not run.

prior_art.found: LiteLLM and the provider SDKs separate rate-limit (429) from service-unavailable/overloaded (5xx/529) errors; the breaker is already subsumed in provider_health/retry.py
prior_art.reused: the existing 'unavailable' kind and breaker; no new dependency or engine state
prior_art.why_custom: a two-line classifier branch plus a pattern; the gap was classification, not retry machinery
